proof.criterion: Review round 3, High (mirror-ci-images.sh:77): round 2's label check fails a row that is labelled correctly, so the ci-images job of this pull request would exit 1 and a re-run would give the same answer
proof.surface: Docker Hub and ghcr.io, read anonymously from the issue pod, and the copy script's own harness
proof.command: An anonymous manifest read of docker.io/library/nats:2.15.1-alpine against the row's digest; then bash .github/scripts/mirror-ci-images.test.sh
proof.observed: The reviewer's reading is confirmed: that tag now resolves elsewhere than the row's correctly pinned sha256:2ae57dfb, so the deleted check would have refused it, and this pull request retags every row, so every tagged row would have reached it. The read is deleted, with its row field, its output lines and the header section that explained them; the header now says why no read of an upstream tag can stand there. The copy itself is unchanged: it reads <the row's upstream>@<the row's digest>, skips a row the package holds at that tag, and refuses a copy that lands elsewhere. The harness prints 32 assertions, 30 before.
proof.negativeControl: The harness keeps the case where the stand-in registry has moved a held row's upstream tag, and that run now passes, which is the behaviour the deleted check got wrong.

proof.criterion: The finding round 2 raised is still answered: a row's label must be held to its bytes, for the versions rule 3 and check-bun-version.sh read from the upstream text
proof.surface: The image's own config, read with crane for every library/golang row, and the build that uses the Bun bytes
proof.command: An anonymous read of each image's config in the pod, then bash .github/scripts/mirror-ci-images.test.sh and bash .github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.sh
proof.observed: library/golang publishes its version: the row's digest carries GOLANG_VERSION=1.27.1 in .config.Env. The copy script now runs `crane config --platform linux/amd64 <upstream>@<row digest>` for every library/golang row, held or copied, and refuses when that version is not the one the row's tag names, naming the row, the version its label claims and the version its bytes carry; it asks for the row's digest and for no tag, so its answer is the same on every day. oven/bun publishes no version anywhere in its config (PATH, BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH, BUN_INSTALL_BIN and nothing else), so the build decides instead: packages/envoy/docker/Dockerfile's web stage copies .bun-version and refuses a `bun --version` that is not its content, before it installs or builds anything, as worker.Dockerfile already does through its build script. .bun-version joined release-envoy-listener.yaml's on.push.paths and ci.yaml's envoy_smoke filter, and check-image-trigger-paths.sh passes with 5 image builds.
proof.negativeControl: Two new harness cases: a held library/golang row whose image carries Go 1.26.3 under a 1.27.1-alpine label fails, naming the row and both versions and copying nothing, and a row whose image carries the Go its tag names passes. The held half is the one the deleted check could never reach.

proof.surface: The gate over fixtures and over the real tree
proof.observed: 99 assertions, 96 before, and the tree mode passes with 12 rows and 35 references. upstream_parts writes out Docker Hub's implicit library/ for the hosts "", docker.io, index.docker.io and registry-1.docker.io and for a repository of one path element, so every rule that compares a repository reads both spellings alike; and the copy script's output sentence describes what the run now prints, one line per held row, two per copied row, one more per library/golang row, then the summary.
proof.negativeControl: The new red case golang-short-spelling: both golang rows respelled without library/ and a FROM moved onto the next-version row; rule 7 fires, and the case also asserts rule 3 reads the pinned row under its short spelling rather than reporting it missing.

proof.criterion: The round's other checks, which these changes could have broken
proof.surface: The repository's own gates, over the real tree
proof.command: bash .github/scripts/check-bun-version.sh ; check-bun-version.test.sh ; check-ci-filters.sh ; check-action-pins.sh ; check-private-names.sh ; a PyYAML parse of every workflow file
proof.observed: `every Bun install reads .bun-version (1.4.4)`; 119 assertions; `every ci.yaml filter matches every file its job reads (25 gates)`; every action pinned; no private name; every workflow parses.
proof.negativeControl: check-ci-filters.sh is the control on the two filter edits: it fails a step whose reads its filter misses, and it passes with .bun-version named in the envoy_smoke filter and in release-envoy-listener.yaml's on.push.paths.

discoveredComplexity: A registry cannot tell a wrong label from a moved tag: both read the same way. Only the image's own metadata, where it publishes a version, or the build that uses the bytes, can bind a row's label to what it carries, and the two images this change pins differ on which of those is available.
